reasoning_traces.think:
Symbolic regression attempts to extract compact formulas from high-dimensional pre-snap NFL data. For EPA prediction, the method collapses to constant values due to minimal signal in pre-snap features—confirmed by the fact that even a 3,000-tree gradient booster explains only 0.8% of variance. This indicates that most EPA variation occurs post-snap. In contrast, drive scoring shows more structure, with a formula derived through GP achieving AUC of 0.5818. The formula involves a trigonometric transformation of field position and distance-to-first-down, suggesting a non-linear relationship between these variables and scoring likelihood. The failure mode lies in overfitting to noise when parsimony is too aggressive, leading to degenerate constants. The method’s success hinges on avoiding leakage and ensuring sufficient signal in the input space.
